passage:
A tree near the park was cut down after a storm. The city left a flat piece of the trunk near the path.
A science teacher brought her class to see it. She showed them the rings inside the wood. Each ring showed one year of growth.
Some rings were wide. Others were narrow. The teacher explained that weather, water, and sunlight could affect how a tree grew.
Students touched the rings and counted them. The tree had lived longer than their school building.
Although the tree was gone, it still had something to teach.
The rings showed that growth leaves marks, even when no one notices year by year.
